study.title: Protocol only: planned review of Alfredson eccentrics versus controls, no results
study.evidence_note: Protocol for a review; no data. Results appeared in Murphy 2019 (BJSM). Doesn't test isometrics.
study.confidence_note: Full protocol read via publisher HTML as paraphrase. PROSPERO number differs within the text. 2019 results paper seen as abstract only.
study.impact_line: A plan, not a finding. Use the 2019 results paper for eccentric-versus-control effects, not this card.
key_findings: Protocol only: no trials included, no effects, no certainty ratings
Plans to compare Alfredson eccentrics with wait-and-see, sham, passive physio and other exercise
Primary outcome VISA-A; pain-only VAS or NRS trials excluded
Isometrics listed as an eligible loading type, but no isometric question is asked
summary: PROSPERO-registered protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs and quasi-RCTs
Adults with mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy over 3 months; insertional excluded
Search: PubMed and two CINAHL platforms to Dec 2017, plus registers and grey literature
RoB 2, random-effects mean differences, GRADE and five pre-set sensitivity analyses planned
Rationale: Alfredson is time-heavy, so an equal but easier protocol would matter
study.bottom_line: This paper holds no evidence on whether eccentrics, or isometrics, work. It sets the rules for the 2019 review. Judge that review on its own results.

design: Systematic review and meta-analysis protocol, PRISMA-P 2015
participants: Excludes insertional AT and other heel pain
intervention: No dose or operational definition given
comparator: Wait-and-see: no active or passive treatment
Sham: non-loading exercise, e.g. calf stretch, balance
Traditional physio: friction, manual therapy, ultrasound, tape
Other exercise: isometric, concentric, isotonic or other loading
methods.follow_up: Final timepoint during the loading programme

results.result: None reported; review not yet done
results.detail: Murphy MC et al. Br J Sports Med 2019;53:1070-7 (PMID 30636702), 7 RCTs. From its PEDro abstract only: vs natural history MD 20.6 VISA-A (11.7 to 29.5; 1 trial); vs traditional physio 17.70 (3.75 to 31.66; 2 trials); vs other exercise -5.65 (-10.51 to -0.79; 3 trials). Authors say they can't be confident in these estimates.

pico.p: Adults with mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy over 3 months
pico.c: Wait-and-see, sham exercise, passive physiotherapy, other exercise protocols
pico.o: VISA-A at final timepoint during loading

limits: Protocol: no results, so nothing to apply clinically
Only PubMed and CINAHL as main databases; no Embase
Pools only the final timepoint, which varies between trials
Missing SDs to be borrowed from other trials
No MCID stated to judge clinical importance

full_text.why: Read in full from the free full text (Springer/BMC HTML, paraphrased by fetch tool). PMC and PubMed pages blocked; record verified via Europe PMC.

how_to_apply: Don't change practice from this paper; it reports no data.
For eccentric-versus-control effects, read Murphy 2019 (BJSM) instead.
For isometrics in early-stage patients, look to isometric trials; this protocol doesn't address them.
applies_to: Understanding how the Murphy 2019 review was designed
Checking that review against its pre-registered plan
not_for: Deciding on isometrics for early or irritable mid-portion pain

appraisal.tool: AMSTAR 2 (critical domains, applied to planned methods only)

domains.reason: PROSPERO number given, written inconsistently; registration date relative to the planned search not stated.
domains.support: Abstract and Methods: CRD42018084493 vs CRD4201804493 in Methods text

domains.reason: Two main databases only, no Embase, but registers, grey literature, citation tracking, hand-searching and experts planned.
domains.support: Search strategy section: PubMed, CINAHL Ovid and EBSCO to 31 Dec 2017

domains.reason: PRISMA flow planned; no commitment to list excluded full texts with reasons.
domains.support: Study selection section: flow diagram only; Not reported

domains.domain: Risk of bias assessed in included studies
domains.reason: RoB 2, two independent reviewers, third arbitrates.
Random-effects MD is fine, but final timepoints of differing length pooled and missing SDs borrowed from other trials.
domains.support: Data synthesis and missing data sections

domains.reason: Pre-set sensitivity analysis removing high-RoB trials; GRADE planned.
domains.support: Sensitivity analysis list item 5; GRADE paragraph

domains.reason: Funnel plot and Egger only if 10+ trials, which is unlikely in this field.
domains.support: Reporting bias section: threshold of 10 studies

grade.reason: Protocol: no included trials to rate.
No evidence body yet; planned PICO is direct for mid-portion AT.

clinical_significance: Protocol names no VISA-A MCID; 6.5 points (McCormack 2015) is a common benchmark
Completed 2019 review: gains vs natural history and passive physio look meaningful, from 1–2 small trials
Its eccentric vs other exercise difference is small and likely trivial
comparator_fairness: Wait-and-see and passive physio are weak comparators, likely to favour any loading
Sham defined as non-loading exercise, which keeps contact time comparable
Other-exercise comparison is the clinically useful one
alternative_explanations: Only planned wait-and-see arms can separate natural history
Pooling different final timepoints may mix short- and longer-term effects
spin: Neutral framing: a question, not a claim
Doesn't over-promise; no results to spin
fit_with_evidence: Murphy 2019 BJSM (abstract level): eccentrics beat natural history and passive physio
Same review: other exercise slightly better than eccentrics, difference likely trivial
Fits the playbook view that loading matters more than the exact protocol
external_validity: ✓ Adults, active or sedentary, mid-portion AT over 3 months
✗ Isometrics only pooled within 'other exercise', if at all
would_change_my_mind: Deviations in the 2019 review from this plan would weaken that review
A full-text read of the 2019 review changing its abstract-level estimates
strengths: Includes wait-and-see and sham comparators missing from earlier reviews
RoB 2, GRADE and pre-set sensitivity analyses planned
No language restriction; grey literature searched
weaknesses: No dose definition of heavy eccentric training
Final timepoints pooled regardless of length
appraisal.funding_conflicts: No study funding stated; BMC waived the open-access fee. Lead author held an Australian Government RTP scholarship. Authors declare no competing interests.

disagreements.why: Registration date vs planned search end not stated.
Authors say they can't be confident in estimates.
Only an Australian scholarship is noted.

disagreements.resolved: Left absent: schema has no 'not applicable'; overall RoB 'not assessable' covers it.

external.rating: High confidence, for the completed 2019 review
external.note: Rates Murphy 2019 BJSM, not this protocol; not comparable with our 'not assessable'.

verification.external_searched: PEDro: 2019 review record 58133, no score; protocol not indexed. Umbrella reviews using AMSTAR 2: Križaj 2022. No Cochrane rating. PMC/PubMed unreachable.

study.patient_explanation: This paper is a plan for a study, not a result. It doesn't tell us which calf exercises work best for your Achilles; the later study it led to suggests most sensible loading programmes help.
open_questions: Did any trial in the 2019 review use isometric loading?
Did the 2019 review follow this plan, e.g. timepoints and SD imputation?
How do isometrics compare with eccentrics in symptoms under 3 months?
What VISA-A MCID did the 2019 review use?

sources.citation: Murphy M, Travers M, Gibson W. Is heavy eccentric calf training superior to wait-and-see, sham rehabilitation, traditional physiotherapy and other exercise interventions for pain and function in mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy? Syst Rev 2018;7:58.
